_readme: Hand-authored English for the Chinese strings of one patent that
resolve_translations.py cannot get any other way. One entry per exact Chinese
string, keyed by the string as the gold spells it, byte for byte.
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: the gold keeps the patent's Chinese, because the Chinese
is the authoritative text and at least one finding in FINDINGS.md was only
catchable by reading it. The consuming team cannot read Chinese. Almost all of
the gap closes from data already in the pipeline: the enriched source carries a
machine translation of nearly every line, and most Chinese aliases sit on a
record that already names the same molecule in English. What is left is the
handful of class terms and misprints that neither can reach.
TRANSLATE THESE AS CHEMISTRY, NOT AS TEXT. Check every name against the
structure or against the context in the patent rather than word by word. There
is no OPSIN and no network here, so nothing verifies a hand-authored name
except a human doing it, and a wrong chemical translation reads exactly as
convincingly as a right one. A wrong translation is worse than an admitted gap:
the gap is visible in the report, the wrong name is not.
PRESERVE THE PATENT'S ERRORS. Where the Chinese itself is wrong, translate the
error faithfully and explain it in 'note'. Silently correcting it would make the
gold agree with chemistry instead of agreeing with the document, which is the
one thing a reference annotation may never do.
WHAT NOT TO PUT HERE: anything the pipeline already resolves. A quotation whose
source line carries a '> EN:' line resolves with origin 'source_mt'. A Chinese
alias of a compound the gold also names in English resolves with origin
'gold_alias'. Both are stronger provenance claims than 'curated', because both
are the document's or the annotation's own words rather than ours. An entry here
for one of those is harmless, and is reported as overridden, but it is work you
did not need to do.
OVERRIDE, and when it is honest to use it. An entry may carry
'override': true, which makes it beat the source and the gold instead of
losing to them. That is normally exactly backwards, because both are
better provenance than we are. The one shape that earns it is a SHORT
PHRASE whose source-line answer is the translation of the WHOLE PARAGRAPH
it was quoted out of. A consumer substitutes the index into the
annotator's English commentary, and a 695-character paragraph spliced into
the middle of a sentence is not a translation of a 14-character phrase, it
is a different and much worse answer. 'override' requires both an 'en' and
a 'note', so the reasoning is attached to the decision in the artifact.
FIELDS: 'en' is the English form and must contain no Chinese. 'note' is free
text and is appended to the entry's note whichever tier ends up supplying the
English, so it is the right place for anything a reader has to know about the
string. Set 'en' to null, with a note, to record a gap deliberately left open:
the coverage gate still reports it, and the reasoning travels with it instead
of being lost.
NOT EVERY ENTRY IS A MOLECULE. [0002] ends with a list of the weeds the
target herbicide controls, and the source's machine translation keeps the
Chinese plant names beside their English glosses, so those runs reach a
screen too and are indexed here. They are translated as botany on the same
terms the compounds are translated as chemistry: against what the name
denotes, with the genus-versus-species distinction the Chinese makes
preserved rather than flattened.
Each name below was worked out from the patent's own context, and the
confidence in each is stated in its note.
alias spellings of the formula (V) acid and the formula (VIII) ester, eight short
provenance quotes, and four fragments the annotator quoted inside English prose.
The other nine exist to keep a qualifier that the gold's own shorter name drops:
a solution strength, anhydrous, glacial. The substance was right in every one of
those nine; what was missing is a fact about what was actually charged.
ONE MISPRINT RECORDED RATHER THAN PROPAGATED: 式(V III)化合物 on line 512 is
printed with a space inside the roman numeral. It is formula (VIII), as the
following line spells it. The English says so and the note keeps the misprint
visible.
ON THIS RUN'S ENTRIES. Seventeen are strings that had no English anywhere: five
alias spellings of the formula (V) acid and the formula (VIII) ester, eight short
provenance quotes, and four fragments the annotator quoted inside English prose.
One more, 冰醋酸, is here because it is glacial acetic acid and not ice acetic acid.
EIGHT ENTRIES WERE WRITTEN AND THEN REMOVED, and the reason is worth keeping. They
translated strings like 20％NaNO2水溶液 and 无水四氢呋喃, which the gold carried as
ALIASES of the pure substance. A curated translation could not fix that: the alias
tier outranks this file, so the index kept resolving them to the bare name and the
name fidelity gate kept failing. The real defect was upstream, in calling a charged
solution or a grade another NAME for the molecule. Those aliases were removed from
the compound records instead, the strength stays in the quantity note and in
purity_pct, and these entries then had nothing left to key on.
fragments such as 式, 权利要求, 其中步骤 and 的一锅法方式实施. They are not names of
anything. They are here because the visual evidence pack quotes drawing labels and
sentence pieces verbatim, and its own gate refuses to let a single Han character
reach a reviewer who cannot read one. Each is translated as the fragment it is,
not as the sentence it came from.

中间体酯化合物.note: an alias on a gold compound record. The 3-oxocyclohex-1-en-1-yl ester of formula (VIII), which the patent calls an intermediate because the route carries it on to tembotrione without isolating it in the one-pot variant.

式(V)羧酸化合物.note: an alias on a gold compound record. Formula (V) is the benzoic acid, 2-chloro-4-(methanesulfonyl)-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]benzoic acid.

式(V)的羧酸化合物.note: an alias on a gold compound record. The same substance as 式(V)羧酸化合物; the patent prints both forms, with and without 的.

式(V III)化合物.note: an alias on a gold compound record. PRINTED WITH A SPACE INSIDE THE NUMERAL, 式(V III), on line 512. It is the formula (VIII) ester: the same compound the next line spells 式(VIII)化合物. Translated to the intended label and the misprint recorded rather than propagated.

式(VIII)酯中间体.note: an alias on a gold compound record. Another of the patent's several spellings for the formula (VIII) enol ester.

水洗.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record.

加水淬灭.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record.

水20g.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record. A charge, not a wash: this is the water that supplies the carboxyl oxygen in the hydroxycarbonylation.

氮气置换.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record. The autoclave is evacuated and its atmosphere replaced with nitrogen before CO is admitted.

加入水.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record.

通入CO.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record. Carbon monoxide admitted to the autoclave under pressure.

如下方法.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record.

如下路线.note: quote_zh on a provenance row, the evidence for a record.

大量.note: a Chinese term quoted inside the annotator's English commentary on a provenance row.

方法.note: a Chinese term quoted inside the annotator's English commentary on a provenance row. Used as the label of the alternative procedures the patent numbers 方法1 and 方法2.

其它与方法.en: the rest being as in Method
其它与方法.note: a Chinese term quoted inside the annotator's English commentary on a provenance row. A fragment of 其它与方法1相同, everything else the same as in Method 1, which is how Example 9's second method inherits the first method's charges.

相同.note: a Chinese term quoted inside the annotator's English commentary on a provenance row.

冰醋酸.note: supplied so the English keeps a qualifier the gold's own shorter name drops. The strength or state is a fact about what was charged, not decoration. 冰 is glacial here, not ice.

式(I)化合物.note: The patent's own label for this compound, rendered as the label it is. OVERRIDE, because the automatic answer was the molecular formula: the gold carries this molecule under several identifiers and the alias tier picked the formula-shaped one. A reviewer reading the claims meets 式(I)化合物 as a LABEL, and 'compound of formula (I)' is what the patent says; the formula is a fact about the molecule, not a translation of its name. Three of the eight labels already resolved this way on their own, so this also makes the eight consistent with each other.
